# 12-Week Hypertrophy Programme — Intermediate Lifter

Below is a structured 12-week hypertrophy block for your client. It uses an **Upper/Lower 4-day split** with progressive volume and intensity across three phases. Rest 60–90s on isolation work, 2–3 min on compound lifts.

---

## Programme Overview

- **Split:** Upper A / Lower A / Upper B / Lower B (4 days/week)
- **Suggested schedule:** Mon / Tue / Thu / Fri
- **Phases:**
  - **Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4):** Accumulation — moderate volume, RPE 7
  - **Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8):** Intensification — higher volume, RPE 7–8
  - **Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12):** Peak & Deload — high intensity, RPE 8–9, deload week 12

Progression: add 2.5–5 kg or 1 rep per set weekly where feasible. Every fourth week (Wk 4, 8) is a lighter accumulation drop before increasing again.

---

## PHASE 1 — Accumulation (Weeks 1–4)

**Focus:** Establish technique, build work capacity, moderate volume. RPE 7 (3 reps in reserve).

# Lean-Mass Gain Nutrition Plan — 12 Weeks

Designed to support the hypertrophy programme above. The goal is **lean tissue accrual with minimal fat gain** — a controlled surplus, high protein, and periodised calorie adjustments across phases.

---

## Baseline Calculations

Since I don't have the client's stats, use these formulas. Adjust once bodyweight and training load are known.

### Step 1 — Maintenance (TDEE)
Use the Mifflin-St Jeor equation, then apply activity multiplier:
- **BMR (male):** (10 × kg) + (6.25 × cm) − (5 × age) + 5
- **Activity multiplier:** 1.55–1.7 for a lifter training 4× plus daily activity (assume 1.6 as default).

### Step 2 — Surplus
- **Lean bulk surplus:** +250–350 kcal/day above TDEE
- **Target rate of gain:** 0.25–0.4% of bodyweight per week (~0.2–0.3 kg/wk for an 80 kg lifter)

**Example — 80 kg, 180 cm, 26 y/o male:**
- BMR ≈ 1,830 kcal
- TDEE (×1.6) ≈ 2,930 kcal
- Lean bulk target ≈ **3,200 kcal/day**

### Step 3 — Macros
| Macro | g/kg bodyweight | % of calories (approx.) |
|---|---|---|
| Protein | 1.8–2.2 g/kg | 25–30% |
| Fat | 0.8–1.0 g/kg | 25–30% |
| Carbohydrate | Fill remainder | 45–50% |

**Example (80 kg, 3,200 kcal):**
- Protein: 175 g (700 kcal)
- Fat: 80 g (720 kcal)
- Carbs: 445 g (1,780 kcal)

---

## Phase-Based Adjustments

Calorie needs increase as bodyweight and training volume rise. Adjust every 2–3 weeks based on scale trend (7-day average) and mirror/measurements.

### Phase 1 — Weeks 1–4 (Accumulation)
- **Calories:** TDEE + 250 kcal
- **Protein:** 1.8–2.0 g/kg
- **Carbs:** Moderate–high, prioritise around training
- **Goal weight gain:** 0.2–0.3 kg/week
- If gain exceeds 0.4 kg/wk for 2 consecutive weeks → reduce carbs by ~30 g/day.

### Phase 2 — Weeks 5–8 (Intensification)
- **Calories:** TDEE + 300–350 kcal (recalculate TDEE using current bodyweight)
- **Protein:** 2.0 g/kg
- **Carbs:** Increase by 30–50 g/day to fuel added volume
- **Goal weight gain:** 0.2–0.3 kg/week
- Monitor waist measurement weekly — if it climbs faster than chest/arms, tighten calories by 150–200.

### Phase 3 — Weeks 9–12 (Peak & Deload)
- **Weeks 9–11:** Maintain surplus (~TDEE + 300 kcal). Peak training demands full fuelling.
- **Week 12 (Deload):** Drop to maintenance (TDEE only). Reduced training volume means reduced energy demand — this prevents unnecessary fat gain during the deload.

---

## Meal Structure

**4–5 meals/day**, spaced 3–4 hours apart. Each meal contains **30–50 g protein** to maximise MPS across the day.

### Sample Day (80 kg lifter, ~3,200 kcal, training PM)

**Meal 1 — Breakfast (7:30 am)**
- 4 whole eggs + 2 egg whites
- 80 g oats (dry weight) with berries
- 1 tbsp peanut butter
- Black coffee

**Meal 2 — Lunch (12:00 pm)**
- 180 g chicken breast
- 250 g cooked rice
- Mixed veg with olive oil (1 tbsp)

**Meal 3 — Pre-workout (4:30 pm, ~90 min pre)**
- 150 g Greek yoghurt
- 1 banana
- 40 g whey protein
- 30 g honey or dates

**Meal 4 — Post-workout (7:30 pm)**
- 200 g lean beef mince (5% fat) or salmon
- 300 g sweet potato or white potato
- Large salad, balsamic + light drizzle olive oil

**Meal 5 — Pre-bed (9:30 pm)**
- 250 g cottage cheese or casein shake
- 30 g almonds or 1 tbsp nut butter

---

## Training-Day vs Rest-Day Structure

Consider a light **calorie/carb cycle** to place more fuel around training:

| Day | Calories | Carbs | Fat |
|---|---|---|---|
| Training days (×4) | +100 kcal above target | Higher (~500 g) | Lower (~70 g) |
| Rest days (×3) | −100 kcal below target | Lower (~380 g) | Higher (~90 g) |

Weekly average stays at the surplus target. Protein stays constant daily.

---

## Nutrient Timing

- **Pre-training:** 30–50 g carbs + 30 g protein, 60–120 min prior.
- **Intra-training (optional):** 20–40 g carbs (e.g. cyclic dextrin, electrolytes) for sessions >75 min.
- **Post-training:** Whole-food meal within 1–2 hours: 40–50 g protein + 80–120 g carbs.
- **Pre-bed:** Slow-digesting protein (casein, cottage cheese, Greek yoghurt) — 30–40 g.

---

## Food Quality Guidelines

**Protein sources:** Chicken breast, lean beef, turkey, white fish, salmon, eggs, Greek yoghurt, cottage cheese, whey/casein.

**Carbohydrate sources:** Oats, rice (white and brown), potatoes, sweet potato, pasta, sourdough, fruit, honey.

**Fat sources:** Olive oil, avocado, nuts, nut butters, whole eggs, oily fish, dark chocolate (85%+).

**Micronutrients:** Aim for **5+ portions** of fruit/veg daily. Include leafy greens, cruciferous veg, and 2 servings of fruit.

**Hydration:** 35–40 ml/kg bodyweight/day (~3 L for an 80 kg lifter). Add 500–750 ml during training.

---

## Supplements (Optional, Evidence-Based)

| Supplement | Dose | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Whey protein | 25–40 g as needed | Convenient protein source |
| Creatine monohydrate | 5 g/day | Strength, hypertrophy, cell hydration |
| Vitamin D3 | 2,000–4,000 IU/day | Hormonal & immune support |
| Omega-3 (EPA/DHA) | 2–3 g/day | Inflammation, recovery |
| Caffeine | 3–5 mg/kg pre-workout | Performance |
| Electrolytes | As needed | Hydration, especially high-sweat sessions |

---

## Monitoring & Adjustment Protocol

- **Weigh-in:** Same time daily (upon waking, after toilet, before food). Use **7-day rolling average**.
- **Body measurements:** Weekly — waist (navel), chest, arms, thighs.
- **Photos:** Every 2 weeks, same lighting/pose.
- **Strength log:** Track top sets each session — steady progression confirms surplus is sufficient.

### Adjustment Rules
- **Gain <0.15 kg/week for 2 consecutive weeks** → add 150 kcal (mostly carbs).
- **Gain >0.4 kg/week for 2 consecutive weeks** → reduce 150 kcal (mostly carbs/fat).
- **Waist gaining faster than limb measurements** → surplus is too high; trim 150–200 kcal.
- **Strength stalling + weight flat** → almost always under-eating; add 200 kcal.

---

## Expected Outcomes Over 12 Weeks

For an intermediate lifter with consistent execution:
- **Bodyweight:** +2.5–3.5 kg total (roughly 65–75% lean mass)
- **Strength:** 5–10% increases across main compounds
- **Waist:** Should stay within +2 cm of starting point

If waist grows faster than that, the surplus is too aggressive — pull calories back.

---

Let me know if you'd like a **structured shopping list**, **meal-prep template**, or a **cut protocol** to follow this block.

# Conditioning Add-On — 2 Sessions/Week

Two conditioning sessions integrated to **preserve hypertrophy adaptations**, improve work capacity and cardiovascular health, and support recovery — without cutting into lifting performance or the calorie surplus.

---

## Placement in the Weekly Schedule

| Day | Session |
|---|---|
| Mon | Upper A |
| Tue | Lower A |
| **Wed** | **Conditioning 1 — Low-Intensity Steady State (LISS)** |
| Thu | Upper B |
| Fri | Lower B |
| **Sat** | **Conditioning 2 — High-Intensity Intervals (HIIT)** |
| Sun | Rest |

**Rationale:**
- LISS on Wednesday sits between lower-body days as active recovery.
- HIIT on Saturday is placed **at least 24 h after Lower B** and before a full rest day, so it doesn't interfere with heavy squat/deadlift performance.
- Never do HIIT the day before or after a lower-body lift.

---

## Session 1 — LISS (Wednesday)

**Purpose:** Aerobic base, recovery, capillary density, fat oxidation. Low systemic fatigue.

2. **Week 8 was already a drop week.** The original programme built in a lower-fatigue week exactly where we now need one. We're using existing programme structure, not adding to it.
3. **Phase 3 opens with a rep-range shift (from 6s to 5s).** That transition naturally recalibrates loads. She doesn't need to have hit her theoretical Week 8 numbers to hit her Week 9 numbers — Phase 3 has its own load progression logic.

---

## Nutrition Through the Ramp

- **Week 7R:** full Phase 2 surplus (TDEE + 300–350 kcal). Fuelling supports adaptation, not just training energy expenditure.
- **Week 8:** same surplus. Expect a small bodyweight uptick as glycogen refills from resumed high-carb training days — this is not fat gain, don't react to it.
- **Weeks 9–11:** full Phase 3 surplus as originally planned.
- **Week 12:** drop to maintenance for the deload as originally planned.

---

## Tracking Metrics That Matter Now

For the next three weeks, watch these more closely than usual:

- **Top-set bar speed** (visual — if it's grinding, load is too high)
- **Session-to-session RPE trend** (should feel *easier* each week if recovery is on track)
- **Morning HR** (creeping upward = under-recovered)
- **Bodyweight 7-day average** (should resume upward drift by end of Week 8)

If three of these four are trending correctly by end of Week 8, she's on the original trajectory. Phase 3 as written.

---

# 12-Week Hypertrophy Programme — Final Consolidated Version

Full programme integrating: Upper/Lower 4-day split, conditioning, lean-mass nutrition, the Weeks 5–6 hotel dumbbell travel block, the Week 7 reintroduction, the Week 8 bridge, and the original Phase 3 peak/deload.

---

## Programme Overview

- **Split:** Upper A / Lower A / Upper B / Lower B (4 days/week)
- **Conditioning:** 2 sessions/week (Wed LISS, Sat HIIT)
- **Weekly schedule:** Mon / Tue / Wed / Thu / Fri / Sat / Sun rest

| Week | Phase | Focus |
|---|---|---|
| 1–4 | Phase 1 — Accumulation | Technique, work capacity, RPE 7 |
| **5–6** | **Travel Block — DB Only** | **Hold hypertrophy, RPE 8–9** |
| **7** | **Reintroduction (7R)** | **Rebuild barbell skill, RPE 7** |
| **8** | **Bridge** | **Return to pre-travel loads + small bump, RPE 8** |
| 9–11 | Phase 3 — Peak | High intensity, RPE 8–9 |
| 12 | Deload | 60–65% loads, RPE 5–6 |

---

## Weekly Schedule (All Weeks)

| Day | Session |
|---|---|
| Mon | Upper A |
| Tue | Lower A |
| Wed | LISS (30–45 min, Zone 2) |
| Thu | Upper B |
| Fri | Lower B |
| Sat | HIIT (15–20 min working time) |
| Sun | Rest |

---

# PHASE 1 — Accumulation (Weeks 1–4)

**Focus:** Establish technique, moderate volume, RPE 7. Rest 2–3 min compounds, 60–90s isolation.

### Upper A

| Chest-Supported Row | 4 × 10 |

| Lat Pulldown | 3 × 12 |

### Lower A
| Exercise | Sets × Reps |

| Leg Extension | 3 × 12 |
| Seated Leg Curl | 3 × 12 |
| Standing Calf Raise | 4 × 12 |
| Hanging Knee Raise | 3 × 12 |

### Upper B
| Exercise | Sets × Reps |

- **Wk 1:** baseline loads, RPE 7
- **Wk 2:** +1 rep per set or +2.5 kg
- **Wk 3:** +1 rep per set or +2.5 kg
- **Wk 4:** hold loads, drop 1 set from each accessory (drop week)

### Phase 1 Conditioning
- **Wed LISS:** 30 min incline walk / Zone 2 bike, 60–70% max HR
- **Sat HIIT:** 30s hard / 90s easy × 6 rounds on assault bike or rower (RPE 8)

---

# TRAVEL BLOCK — Weeks 5–6 (Hotel DBs Only)

**Intent:** Hold hypertrophy. Volume ~10 hard sets/muscle/week, RPE 8–9, frequency preserved.

**Load principles:**
- Rep ranges 8–15 primary
- 3s eccentrics on compounds
- Every last set to RPE 8–9
- If DBs feel light: add reps → slow tempo → add sets (in that order)

## Week 5

| Hollow Body Hold | 3 × 30s |

- **Sat HIIT:** 40s / 20s × 4 rounds — burpees, mountain climbers, jump squats, high knees

## Week 6

Same exercises as Week 5, **increased demand**:
- Add 2 reps to each working set, OR
- Add a drop set (drop 20–30%, AMRAP) on the final set of each compound, OR
- Add 10 partials on the final set of each isolation

- **Upper A:** DB Bench 4 × 12 + drop set • Lat Raise 4 × 20 with 1½ reps final
- **Lower A:** Goblet Squat 5 × 12 • Bulgarian SS 3 × 12/leg + 5 bottom-half pulses
- **Upper B:** OHP 5 × 8 • Incline Bench 4 × 12 + drop set • Lat/Rear Delt 4 × 15 each
- **Lower B:** DB Deadlift 5 × 8 • Hip Thrust 4 × 15 with 2s top squeeze • Reverse Lunge 3 × 12/leg

- **Sat HIIT:** Same bodyweight circuit, **5 rounds**

**Intent:** Return to full pre-travel working loads with a small top-set progression to confirm neural readiness. Uses the original Week 8 drop-week structure (accessories −1 set) which conveniently limits fatigue.
